topPRs.title: Refresh the smart contract architecture overview
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
The overview still used the older dispute-game contracts and omitted the L2 contract upgrade path. Update the L1 diagrams for U20 with ETHLockbox enabled, and document the Karst L2 upgrade flow.

- Show super-root games, withdrawal validation, ETH custody, and the correct pause and owner permissions.
- Add the L2ContractsManager upgrade flow and supporting predeploys, OperatorFeeVault, and beacon-root and block-history notes.
- Separate dense diagrams by purpose, use consistent colors, and move pause and permission details into nearby notes. Correct the ERC721 bridge labels and distinguish fixed implementations from upgradeable proxies.

Validation: Markdown, table-of-contents, spelling and filename checks, book build, and overview links. Reviewed all seven rendered diagrams in light and dark themes.

CircleCI `lint-specs` and `build-book` passed.

topPRs.title: lagoon: specify post-exec receipt JSON-RPC fee fields
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
## Why

Closes part of [protocol-team#333](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/333) (DoD items 1 and 2).

The post-exec (`0x7D`) § Receipt section pinned only the **consensus** RLP fields. The OP-specific fee fields a client surfaces over JSON-RPC were left unspecified, so op-reth derives `l1Fee` and `l1GasUsed` from the post-exec transaction's encoding like any other non-deposit transaction. On sdm-net-0 a fee-less transaction therefore reports a non-zero L1 fee:

```jsonc
{
  "type": "0x7d",
  "gasUsed": "0x0",
  "effectiveGasPrice": "0x0",
  "l1Fee": "0x1ae917a28",   // <- fee-less tx, non-zero fee
  "l1GasUsed": "0x640"
}
```

That is misleading for explorers, indexers and fee accounting that sum L1 fees across a block's receipts.

## What

§ Receipt is split into **Consensus Fields** (unchanged text) and a new **JSON-RPC Fields** subsection, which specifies the fee fields in the two groups they naturally fall into:

- **Transaction-scoped** — what *this* transaction was charged. A post-exec transaction is charged nothing, so `gasUsed`, `effectiveGasPrice`, `l1Fee`, `l1GasUsed` and `blobGasUsed` MUST each be present and zero. `cumulativeGasUsed` is called out separately since it is block-cumulative and inherits the preceding receipt's value. `opGasRefund` MUST be absent or `null`.
- **Block-scoped** — the block's L1 fee parameters, read from the L1 attributes deposit. `l1GasPrice`, `l1BaseFeeScalar`, `l1BlobBaseFee`, `l1BlobBaseFeeScalar`, `operatorFeeScalar`, `operatorFeeConstant` and `daFootprintGasScalar` MUST match every other receipt in the same block in both value and presence. `l1FeeScalar` is pre-Ecotone only, so a post-exec receipt never reports it.

## Zeroed, not omitted

The issue raised omitting `l1Fee`/`l1GasUsed` instead, on the grounds that deposit (`0x7E`) receipts omit them. That precedent only holds for op-geth: `deriveOPStackFields` skips deposits entirely, so the fields are `nil` and drop out of the JSON. op-reth does **not** — a `0x7E` receipt on sdm-net-0 reports `l1Fee: "0x0"` and a *non-zero* `l1GasUsed: "0x738"`, since only `l1_tx_data_fee` takes the `is_deposit` flag and `l1_data_gas` does not.

So there is no single existing deposit shape to follow. This spec zeroes instead, which:

- keeps a post-exec receipt the same shape as a regular transaction's receipt;
- matches `gasUsed` and `effectiveGasPrice`, already present-and-zero on these receipts;
- lets a consumer sum `l1Fee` over a block's receipts and reach the right total with no special case and no key-existence check.

`l1GasUsed: 0` is also consistent with [§ DA Footprint](https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/lagoon/post-exec.html#da-footprint), which already requires clients to treat a post-exec transaction's DA footprint as zero and its `blobGasUsed` as zero.

## Notes

- The block-scoped half is already the observed behaviour on sdm-net-0 — every one of those fields matches the regular receipts in the same block, and `blobGasUsed` is already `0x0`. Specifying it locks that in rather than changing it.
- A deposit receipt's `l1Fee`/`l1GasUsed` shape still differs between op-geth (omitted) and op-reth (present, and `l1GasUsed` non-zero). That is pre-existing and out of scope here, but worth its own ticket.

Implementation: ethereum-optimism/optimism#22941 (op-reth).

topPRs.title: docs(superchain-upgrades): disallow simultaneous upgrade activations
topPRs.author: OptimismBot
topPRs.body:
Adds a general activation rule: two network upgrades MUST NOT activate at the same L2 block timestamp, unless that timestamp is at or before genesis (where upgrades activate in the genesis block itself and conventionally share timestamp `0`).

The restriction was already real but undocumented — nothing in the specs constrained activation-time ordering, and [`checkFork`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-node/rollup/types.go#L465-L480) in op-node explicitly permits equality. [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22828](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22828) is what surfaced it: Karst and Lagoon activating at the same non-genesis timestamp both add upgrade gas, but the reconstruction helpers only subtract Karst's allocation, so the inflated gas limit persists.

Per the thread discussion, the rule is stated once under "Activation rules" rather than repeated in each fork's own specification. Rationale captured in the text: each upgrade's activation-block behavior is only defined against a chain where every prior upgrade is active and every later one is not, so supporting overlapping activations would mean specifying and testing every combination of upgrades that could activate together.

The wording is scoped to OP-Stack network upgrades — it deliberately does not constrain an OP-Stack upgrade timestamp against an L1 fork timestamp on the same chain (e.g. Upgrade 15 sets `pragueTime == isthmusTime`).

The second commit adds a non-retroactivity note, because six chains in the superchain registry already violate the rule: Celo mainnet activated Holocene and Isthmus at `1752073200` (genesis `1742957258`), and sepolia/boba, sepolia/lisk, sepolia/mode, sepolia/race and sepolia/soneium-minato each share a post-genesis timestamp between two earlier upgrades. Their activation history cannot be changed, so the rule has to bind newly scheduled activations rather than all historical configs.

Companion monorepo PR — docs plus the strengthened rollup-config validation: [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22838](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22838)

Prompted by: @sebastianst
